designationHistory.name: Cherokee National Game Refuge No. 2
designationHistory.indexText: President Coolidge set aside Cherokee National Game Refuges Numbers One and Two on Weeks Act lands in Tennessee and Georgia; No. 2 was the Georgia refuge.

authority.citation: Proclamation of Aug. 5, 1924, 43 Stat. 1964 (under Act of Aug. 11, 1916, 39 Stat. 446, 476)

sources.name: American Presidency Project (UC Santa Barbara), Proclamation 1707, Setting Aside Cherokee National Game Refuges Numbers One and Two
Proclamation 2287 of June 6, 1938, 52 Stat. 1549, reciting Refuge No. 2 in Georgia (govinfo)

designationHistory.indexText: President Franklin D. Roosevelt renamed Cherokee National Game Refuge No. 2 in Georgia the Noontootly National Game Refuge and redrew its boundaries.

sources.name: American Presidency Project (UC Santa Barbara), Proclamation 2287, Noontootly National Game Refuge, Georgia
